s: Today we talk about health and the body.
Your body is with you every day, so let's take good care of it.
Your body is your arms, your legs, your head, and everything inside you.
Your body needs food and water.
When you take care of your body, you feel strong and happy.
And your brain is part of your body.
Your brain is inside your head.
Your brain helps you think, learn, and remember.
When you learn a new word, your brain keeps it for you.
Your brain works hard all day, so give it rest.
A quiet walk helps your brain, too.
Blood is the red liquid inside your body.
Your blood moves all around your body.
It takes food to your brain and to every part of your body.
When you run, your blood moves fast.
When you rest, your blood moves slow.
Good food and water help your blood stay healthy, and a healthy body feels good.
When I have a headache, I take an aspirin.
An aspirin is a small medicine for pain.
One aspirin can help a headache go away.
But remember, an aspirin is medicine.
Take only one aspirin, and drink water with it.
If the pain stays, see a doctor.
Never take medicine without asking an adult first.

Now, my friend Sara has asthma.
Asthma makes it hard to breathe.
When asthma comes, Sara uses her inhaler, and then she can breathe well again.
Asthma does not stop Sara from playing.
She runs and laughs, and she takes care of her body.
She knows her body well, and she knows what helps her breathe.
Let's finish with three easy tips.
One, drink water for your body and your blood.
Two, sleep well for your brain.
Three, move your body every day.
Your brain, your blood, and your body work together.
Take care of them, and they take care of you.
If you have asthma, keep your inhaler with you.
And if you need an aspirin, ask an adult first.

Your body is everything you are.
Blood moves all around your body.
